# Decision points

Every decision point mu has, 38 in all, grouped as the desktop app's settings group them. Each is asked as a short question about a small state; [How mu works](../architecture.md) explains the engine and [Judges](../judges.md) who answers.

Each point has a mode:

- `active`: The verdict takes effect.
- `shadow`: Asked and recorded, but nothing changes. For watching how well it judges first.
- `off`: Not asked; this decision is off.

Every point is `active` unless set otherwise (`"modes": { "default": "active" }` is the built-in default). Set `"default": "shadow"`, or a point's own mode, in `~/.mu/agent/mu.json` to only record verdicts; the desktop app's settings switch a point on or off; `/mu mode <point|default> <off|shadow|active>` switches one for the current session. See [Configuration](../configuration.md).

The feature column names the switch in `features` that turns the whole behaviour off; its options are in [Features](features.md).

## Input

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input.preflight` | Message preflight | Classifies each message and how much thinking it needs, then gives a one-line hint; optionally sets the turn's thinking level. | [`preflight`](features.md#preflight) |
| `task.frame` | Task frame update | Asks of each message: a new task, a new hard constraint, a correction, a new subgoal, or no change. Only a change has a model rewrite the task frame. | [`frame`](features.md#frame) |
| `input.interjection` | Mid-run messages | A message that arrives while the agent works: interrupt now, or handle it after the current step. | [`interjection`](features.md#interjection) |

## Context

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skills.disclosure` | Skill disclosure | Only skills relevant to the task go into the prompt; the rest stay hidden but findable. | [`skills`](features.md#skills) |
| `capability.disclosure` | Capability disclosure | Packs and MCP servers are installed but hidden, opened only when a task needs them; their processes start then. | [`catalog`](features.md#catalog) |
| `tool.admission` | Tool output admission | Long tool output is judged in chunks; only what matters enters the context, the rest is archived with a pointer. | [`admission`](features.md#admission) |
| `tool.admission.test-log` | Test log trimming | Exact repeats in test output are kept once; optionally the judge selects what is needed from the rest. | [`admission`](features.md#admission) |
| `context.forget` | Forgetting stale results | When context use crosses a threshold, stale tool results are replaced by one-line tombstones in outgoing requests. | [`forgetting`](features.md#forgetting) |
| `context.compact` | Summary-free compaction | Compaction keeps or prunes passages by judgment instead of asking a model for a summary. | [`compaction`](features.md#compaction) |
| `memory.recall` | Lesson recall | Picks the lessons relevant to the current task and brings them into the turn. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.capture` | Lesson capture | Decides whether a message of yours corrects the agent or sets a rule for later; if so, it becomes a lesson. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.outcome` | Learning from a way out | When the agent went in circles or off course and the turn still ended with a passing check or the goal met, judges whether what finally worked was a different approach; if so, keeps the trap and the way around it. Asked at most once a turn. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.worth` | Worth keeping | For a lesson the model keeps with the remember tool, or a Lesson: line in a sub-agent's report: useful again later, a one-off, or known already from the prompt or the project files. Only the first kind is kept. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.merge` | Lesson merging | Before a new lesson is stored, compares it with the most similar kept ones: the same lesson is not kept twice, a more precise one replaces the old, and on a contradiction your latest word wins. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `memory.applied` | Lesson followed | At the end of a turn, judges whether the lessons brought into it were followed. A lesson recalled many times and never followed is retired. | [`memory`](features.md#memory) |
| `cache.warming` | Cache warming | Guesses whether you will be back soon, to decide on refreshing the prompt cache before it expires. | [`warming`](features.md#warming) |

## Tools and safety

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.risk` | Risky command guard | Rules flag dangerous-looking commands; the judge only vouches that you asked for it. Unsure means asking you. | [`guard`](features.md#guard) |
| `tool.approval` | Jev approves for you | In Jev-approves mode, commands, changes outside the project, outside actions and sub-agents go to Jev first: only what it is sure the task needs, done as you would expect, runs without you; anything else asks you in the status bar. | [`permissions`](features.md#permissions) |
| `tool.constraint` | Hard constraint gate | What you ruled out is kept word for word in the task frame; before a call that changes something, each constraint is checked, and only a confident violation is stopped, in your own words. | [`constraints`](features.md#constraints) |
| `tool.injection` | Instructions in outside content | Before the model reads a web page, search results or an MCP server's answer: which passages carry instructions aimed at an AI (ignore rules, hand over data, run commands, or carry the conversation out through a link)? Those are withheld and replaced by a one-line note. When Jev gives no answer, only plain injection phrases are withheld. | [`injection`](features.md#injection) |
| `files.locate` | File location | Describe what you are looking for; the judge ranks candidate files instead of a string of greps. | [`locate`](features.md#locate) |
| `judge.items` | Judging many items (a tool for the model) | When the model has to sort hundreds of files, log lines or findings, it hands Jev one yes/no question to answer item by item, with a probability each, instead of reading them all. It appears only when a task needs it. The model asked, so it answers in shadow too; off turns it away. | [`judgeItems`](features.md#judgeitems) |
| `browser.step` | Browser steps | Each browser step is observe, one judgment, act: the judge picks the next operation and its target. | [`browser`](features.md#browser) |
| `review.triage` | Review triage | After the reviewer of /review reports, each finding gets two questions: does it change how the program behaves, and is it about this change; with the reviewer's own severity that orders them P0 to P3. None is dropped, P3 is collapsed, and a finding the reviewer insisted on never lands in P3. | [`packs`](features.md#packs) |
| `diagnostics.delivery` | When to tell diagnostics | New language-server diagnostics after an edit: tell now, when the model pauses, or never (style warnings). New errors still there when the turn ends are always told. | [`lsp`](features.md#lsp) |

## Turn

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn.drift` | Drift monitor | Every few steps, checks that the work still serves the goal; rules catch going in circles. | [`monitor`](features.md#monitor) |
| `turn.rewind` | Judged rewind | When the monitor sees the agent going in circles, or one command failing again and again, judges whether the approach is a dead end; only a confident dead end with no progress proposes going back to the turn's checkpoint. It never rewinds by itself. | [`checkpoint`](features.md#checkpoint) |
| `turn.completion` | Completion check | When the model says it is done, checks whether anything verified that; one nudge if not. | [`completion`](features.md#completion) |
| `turn.continue` | Stopped short | A run that ends on "next I'll run the tests" without doing it, or asks for a go-ahead on work you already asked for, is sent back to it. A step that is hard to undo or reaches beyond this machine (push, publish, delete, pay) is never pushed. At most twice per message. | [`continuation`](features.md#continuation) |
| `output.drift` | Mid-stream correction (experiment) | While the model writes, the judge reads the tail of its output against your hard constraints and the configured rules every few hundred characters; on a confident violation the output is cut, the rule is named, and the model carries on from there. Runs only with the feature switched on. | [`ttsr`](features.md#ttsr) |
| `goal.met` | Goal reached (Jev fallback) | Goal mode is checked by a model by default; this decision is used when Jev is chosen or the model gives no answer: it reads the closing message for whether the goal holds and whether you are needed. An open acceptance item or an unverified edit always means not yet. | [`goal`](features.md#goal) |
| `board.read` | Plain-language board: where things stand | In a project with the board on, whenever the agent says something, after a check or a ticked acceptance item, every few tool calls, and whenever the agent stops, multiple-choice questions read its phase, the acceptance item it works on and whether it waits for you, and sort what happened since the last board into news and routine. Only something new has a plain-speaking model write the board again and retell the news on the running account; when a run ends, the news of the whole run is picked again for a summing up. | [`board`](features.md#board) |
| `notify.routing` | Notification routing | For events such as the context budget: tell the model now, later, or not at all. | [`notify`](features.md#notify) |

## Teamwork

| Decision point | Name | What it decides | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `swarm.routing` | Sub-agent routing | Picks a role for each delegated task, and a model tier and thinking level by difficulty. | [`swarm`](features.md#swarm) |
| `swarm.patch` | Scope check of a sub-agent's patch | When an isolated sub-agent hands back a patch, judges from the task, the changed paths and the line counts whether it stays within the task and which files look unrelated. One line of advice for the main agent; it never blocks. | [`swarm`](features.md#swarm) |
| `hive.publish` | Hive: publishing findings | Whether a bee's finding is worth putting on the board for the others. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
| `hive.deliver` | Hive: delivery | Whether a finding on the board matters to a bee's current work; only then is it delivered. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
| `hive.relate` | Hive: corrections | What a new finding does to an earlier one on the board: replaces it, contradicts it, supports it, or nothing. A replaced finding goes down and whoever heard it is told; a contradiction keeps both sides for a bee to settle. | [`hive`](features.md#hive) |
